topics.name: Noun or verb: advice/advise, device/devise, practice/practise
Expressions with prepositions (prone to, wary of, under the influence)
Unless, until, as soon as, no sooner ... than

options: My grandmother gave me some good advice.
My grandmother gave me some good advise.
My grandmother gave me a good advices.
questions.rule: Advice (with c) is the noun and is uncountable. Advise (with s) is the verb.

options: Be wary on opinions that flatter you.
Be wary with opinions that flatter you.
Be wary of opinions that flatter you.
questions.rule: The fixed expression is wary of something.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: The expression is a difference of opinion.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: Second conditional: would + base verb: would study.

questions.after: his fame, Aristotle made a silly mistake.
questions.rule: Despite is followed by a noun (his fame). Although needs a full clause.

questions.after: us on how to prepare for the exam.
questions.rule: After will we need a verb: advise (with s). Advice (with c) is a noun.

questions.prompt: Give advice with 'If I were you'.
questions.rule: We give advice with If I were you, I'd + base verb.

chat: When shall we leave for the market?
options: We'll leave as soon as the rain will stop.
We'll leave as soon as the rain stop.
We'll leave as soon as the rain stops.
questions.rule: After as soon as, use the simple present for the future, not will: as soon as the rain stops.

questions.source: If you don't check the facts, you will believe rumours.
options: Unless you don't check the facts, you will believe rumours.
Unless you check the facts, you will believe rumours.
Unless you will check the facts, you will believe rumours.
questions.rule: Unless means if not, so drop the don't: Unless you check.

questions.prompt: Find and fix the 2 errors in this message.
questions.rule: Nouns end in -ice (advice, practice); verbs end in -ise (Practise every day).

options: If I knew the answer, I would tell you.
If I knew the answer, I will tell you.
If I know the answer, I would tell you.
questions.rule: Second conditional: If + simple past, would + base verb.

options: Although the test was hard, but Sameer passed it.
Although the test was hard, Sameer passed it.
Despite the test was hard, Sameer passed it.
questions.rule: Although + clause, then the main clause with no but. Despite cannot take a full clause.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: After will we need the verb devise (to plan). Device is a noun (a tool).

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: After until, use the simple present for a future event. Papa is singular: arrives.
We say an influence on something.
Despite + noun phrase (heavy rain), then the main clause.

chat: What would you do with a time machine?
options: I will visited the age of the dinosaurs.
I would visit the age of the dinosaurs.
I would visited the age of the dinosaurs.
questions.rule: An imagined situation: would + base verb: I would visit.

chat: Why are you here so early, Sahil?
options: I have come for practise, sir.
I have come for practice, sir.
I has come for practice, sir.
questions.rule: After for we need the noun practice (with c), and I takes have.

questions.source: Riya was tired. She finished her homework.
options: Although Riya was tired, but she finished her homework.
Although Riya is tired, she finished her homework.
Although Riya was tired, she finished her homework.
questions.rule: Although + clause, then the main clause with no but. Both clauses stay in the past.

questions.prompt: Find and fix the 2 errors in this message.
questions.rule: We say afraid of. After a preposition like of, use the -ing form: wary of talking.

options: The prophetess took advantage on her followers.
The prophetess took advantage of her followers.
The prophetess took advantage at her followers.
questions.rule: The fixed expression is take advantage of someone.

options: Until you admit your fears, you cannot conquer them.
Unless you don't admit your fears, you cannot conquer them.
Until you won't admit your fears, you cannot conquer them.
questions.rule: Until takes the simple present for the future, and unless is never used with don't.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: A full clause (he was very tired) needs Although. Despite takes a noun or -ing form.

questions.after: you, I would read a different newspaper for a change.
questions.rule: For an imaginary situation, use If I were you with would.
The subject of a sentence is a noun: practice (with c). Practise (with s) is the verb.
Unless means if not: Don't believe rumours unless you check them.

chat: Did the cricket match go ahead yesterday?
options: Yes, it was played despite of the rain.
Yes, it was played although the rain.
Yes, it was played in spite of the rain.
questions.rule: Say in spite of or despite (never despite of) before a noun. Although needs a clause.

chat: Why do you look worried, Pooja?
options: I'm afraid from the science test tomorrow.
I'm afraid of the science test tomorrow.
I'm afraid with the science test tomorrow.
questions.rule: The adjective afraid is followed by of: afraid of the test.

questions.source: I don't have a car, so I can't drive you home.
options: If I had a car, I could drive you home.
If I have a car, I could drive you home.
If I had a car, I can drive you home.
questions.rule: An unreal present: If + simple past (had), could/would + base verb.

questions.prompt: Find and fix the 3 errors in this message.
questions.rule: Noun: advice. Verbs: She advises (with -s for she) and to practise (with s).

options: Fear causes superstition; however, courage defeats it.
Fear cause superstition; however, courage defeats it.
Fear causes superstition; however, courage defeat it.
questions.rule: However after a semicolon joins two clauses; each singular subject (fear, courage) takes a verb with -s.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: After would, use the base verb: would be much warmer.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: No sooner is a comparative, so it pairs with than, never then or when.
The fixed expression is under the influence of.
Second conditional question: If + were, then wh-word + would + subject + base verb.

chat: Why did you carry an umbrella? It's sunny!
options: The forecast said it might rain, so I brought it.
The forecast said it might rain, so I brings it.
The forecast said it might rain, despite I brought it.
questions.rule: So joins a reason to its result, and the story stays in the past: so I brought it.

options: Let's wait until Mummy will come home.
Let's wait unless Mummy comes home.
Let's wait until Mummy comes home.
questions.rule: Until (up to the time) + simple present for the future: until Mummy comes.

questions.source: As soon as the prophetess spoke, the crowd replied.
options: No sooner the prophetess spoke than the crowd replied.
No sooner did the prophetess spoke than the crowd replied.
No sooner did the prophetess speak than the crowd replied.
questions.rule: No sooner + did + subject + base verb + than: No sooner did the prophetess speak than.

questions.source: Although he was afraid, Raj went into the dark room.
options: Despite he was afraid, Raj went into the dark room.
Despite being afraid, Raj went into the dark room.
Despite of being afraid, Raj went into the dark room.
questions.rule: Despite + -ing form (being afraid). It never takes a full clause or of.

questions.prompt: Find and fix the 2 errors in this message.
questions.rule: After would and will, use the base verb: would travel, will never know.

options: Were I a scientist, I would test every claim myself.
Were I a scientist, I would tested every claim myself.
Was I a scientist, I would test every claim myself.
questions.rule: Were I ... is a formal way to say If I were ..., followed by would + base verb.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: In spite of is followed by a noun or an -ing form: In spite of feeling afraid.
Hardly pairs with when; No sooner pairs with than.
The verb guard takes against: guard yourself against a danger.
No sooner had + subject + past participle + than + simple past.

chat: Would you trust someone who promised to turn silver into gold?
options: Of course not. If someone said that, I will call the police.
Of course not. If someone says that, I would call the police.
Of course not. If someone said that, I would call the police.
questions.rule: An imagined situation: If + simple past (said), would + base verb (would call).

questions.source: Fear causes superstition. It also causes cruelty.
options: Fear causes not only superstition and also cruelty.
Fear causes not only superstition but also cruelty.
Fear causes not only superstition but cruelty also causes.
questions.rule: Not only and but also stand before matching parts: not only superstition but also cruelty.

questions.source: Rahul isn't careful, so he makes silly errors.
options: If Rahul is careful, he would not make silly errors.
If Rahul were careful, he would not make silly errors.
If Rahul were careful, he would not made silly errors.
questions.rule: An unreal present: If + were, would not + base verb: would not make.

questions.source: As soon as the bell rang, the students rushed out.
options: Hardly had the bell rung when the students rushed out.
Hardly had the bell rang when the students rushed out.
Hardly the bell had rung than the students rushed out.
questions.rule: Hardly had + subject + past participle (rung) + when + simple past.

questions.prompt: Find and fix the 3 errors in this message.
questions.rule: A wise person checks; Despite + noun phrase; would have avoided needs if he had asked.
